financial_anchor.metric: FY2026 revenue and GAAP operating income
financial_anchor.caveat: Reported/adjusted measures differ; cycle, mix and capital intensity confound.

ai_claim.claim: Microsoft reported more than 30m paid Microsoft 365 Copilot seats and strong Azure AI demand; controlled end-to-end productivity and own-use cash remain unreported.
ai_claim.stage: E2 external Azure AI demand in opened FY2026 results; own-productivity evidence remains E1
ai_claim.scope: Specific workflow only; infrastructure demand is separated from own productivity.
ai_claim.limitation: No representative controlled cohort or retained-cash reconciliation.

strongest_counterevidence.claim: calendar-2026 AI infrastructure spending was reported near $175bn.
strongest_counterevidence.limitation: Does not itself disprove the scoped mechanism.

rights_limit: Public terms do not prove universal training or pooled cross-customer reuse; enterprise schedules were unavailable.
materiality_summary: $7.76bn = 5% of FY2026 GAAP operating income of $155.2bn. The internal bridge uses an explicitly assumed $80bn annual own operating-expense pool for Microsoft 365/Azure support and development; it excludes revenue.

arithmetic.inputs: assumed $80bn annual own operating-expense pool for Microsoft 365/Azure support and development; efficiency 10%; realization 50%; retained share 40%; recurring cost $3bn
arithmetic.formula: eligible cost × efficiency × realization × retained share − recurring AI expense
